args.query: quote latency deadline exceeded market data slow
redis cache eviction memory key evicted ttl

events.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency was flat at ~60ms until the 13:20 10-min bucket, then jumped abruptly to ~1800ms avg (max 2309.91ms) and has been declining slowly since (last bucket 1171.7ms).
pricing-engine ERRORs are all of the form 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms', first seen 13:23:57 with values from 827ms up to 8456ms; 192 such errors.
redis-cache logged an ERROR at 13:22:10: 'node redis-cache-2 failed health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts); marking primary as down'.
redis-cache logged at 13:22:52 a failover promoting an EMPTY replica: 'failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)'.
redis-cache hit ratio dropped from ~95.8% (13:10 bucket) to 29.06% avg (13:20 bucket) and 15.9% (13:30 bucket), recovering gradually to 46.16% by 14:50.

market-data-service WARN logs are dominated (289) by 'cache miss storm: quote:<id> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (<n>ms)', first seen 13:22:25, with rebuild times of 1-8.7s.
market-data-service p99 latency was flat ~39ms until 13:10, then jumped in the 13:20 bucket to avg 1535.72ms (max 1979.98ms), tracking the pricing-engine degradation.

exchange-gateway p99 latency stayed flat at ~127-133ms across the entire window including the incident period (e.g. 13:20 avg 132.17, 13:30 avg 131.23), so the upstream exchange feed itself was not slow.
redis-cache cpu_pct stayed flat ~22% through the incident (13:20 avg 21.85, 13:30 avg 21.68) and evictions_per_min stayed flat ~3/min (13:20 avg 2.91, 13:30 avg 3.03).

redis-cache memory_pct FELL during the incident rather than rising: 70.34% at 13:00, down to avg 9.32% at 13:30, i.e. the datastore emptied out (consistent with an empty promoted replica, not memory pressure).

The only deployment across all services in the window is auth-service v7.2.0 ('Session cookie hardening') at 11:30:00Z; no deployments exist for market-data-service or redis-cache (count 0 each), and the listing was marked partial.
No configuration or feature-flag changes were recorded for any service, including redis-cache, in the window (count 0, scope all services and redis-cache).
redis-cache logged client reconnect storms after the failover: 15048 new connections in 10s at 13:30:20 and 92851 at 13:40:15, indicating clients thundering back to the new primary.

The failure originated in redis-cache infrastructure (primary node health-check failure forcing promotion of an unsynced/empty replica), not in pricing-engine or market-data-service; those services only reflected the resulting cache-miss latency.
